subject: Clarify: regional pinning scope, temporary cross-hop window, and subprocessor termination notice
messages:
From: Anna Kaufmann <anna.kaufmann@medsys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedSys Health Legal <dpa@medsys-legal.eu>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Regional pinning follow-up + question on termination window

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked strong. Before we move a pilot forward, legal has a couple of concrete asks on residency and subprocessors:

1) When you say "EU region pinning" in the DPA, can you confirm whether that covers both compute and transient cache/edge copies? Our privacy team needs explicit language about ephemeral caches and KV cache replication.

2) If Redwood needs to change a subprocessor that could impact our EU-only routing (for example a replacement that has US-based components), what notice and termination rights do we have? We typically require a 60-day notice and a right to terminate if a suitable EU-only subprocessor is not available.

3) We also have a short cross-hop allowance question: for DR and failover, is there a bounded temporary cross-region processing window (e.g., 72h) and how is that documented/audited?

Can you point me to the exact text in the DPA and any operational playbooks that describe the policy? We're preparing our procurement redlines and want to be concrete.

Best,
Anna
Anna Kaufmann
Sr. Privacy Counsel, MedSys Health
anna.kaufmann@medsys.com
+49 30 555 1212

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kaufmann <anna.kaufmann@medsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 10:35:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Regional pinning follow-up + question on termination window

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Quick replies inline, and we'll follow with a DPA excerpt and our playbook.

1) EU pinning scope: our standard "region pinning" covers primary compute (model hosting + inference) and persistent storage paths. We also treat ephemeral KV/prefix caches as "pinned" when customers enable EU-only cache mode; by default edge caches may be globally distributed for latency-sensitive reads but we can opt them out. We'll attach a short playbook excerpt showing the cache behavior and telemetry keys.

2) Subprocessor changes: standard process is 30 days notice for routine subprocessor swaps and 60 days for changes that would materially alter data residency. For customers requiring contractual 60-day notice + termination right, we can offer a DPA addendum that: (a) guarantees 60-day notice for residency-impacting changes; and (b) provides a termination right if no EU-only alternative is available within the notice period. We'll mark that as an addendum option in the attached DPA draft.

3) Cross-hop/dr DR window: our default bounded failover window is 72 hours for transient cross-region processing; it is logged and flagged as an exception in the customer's audit trail. For customers needing a shorter window or different SLAs, we can set a custom failover policy and require Ops runbook sign-off.

I'll loop in Ben on the onboarding/ops evidence side and Marissa for commercial terms.

Action from Redwood: attach redlined DPA excerpt, the subprocessor roster, and our pinning playbook draft.

--
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Customer Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Subject: internal: suggested DPA language and ops evidence

Irene / Marissa — notes for the reply:

- For Anna's first ask, we should be explicit that "ephemeral KV cache entries" are treated as in-scope when EU-only cache mode is enabled; add a short appendix showing the telemetry keys (cache_region=eu; cache_ttl_max=24h) and where we store exceptions.
- On subprocessors: propose we offer two commercial tracks in the SOW: (1) Standard — 30d notice; (2) Residency Commitment — 60d notice + termination right. For Residency Commitment customers we'll include escrowed subprocessor rosters and monthly attestations.
- For the 72h failover: Ops can produce a signed runbook and an automated incident log that timestamps any cross-hop event. Offer to include 90-day rolling export of cross-region access logs for their security team.

Also, attach a draft DPA snippet that includes the addendum option. I'll prepare the subprocessor csv for Anna.

Ben

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kaufmann <anna.kaufmann@medsys.com>, MedSys Health Legal <dpa@medsys-legal.eu>

Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 08:45:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Regional pinning follow-up + question on termination window

Hi Anna / MedSys Legal — attaching the requested artifacts and a proposed commercial option. Key points summarized below and the attachments contain the contract language and operational evidence templates.

Summary: 
- EU pinning: primary compute + persistent storage are in scope by default. Ephemeral caches are included only when EU-only cache mode is enabled; otherwise edge caches may briefly serve reads from distributed POPs.
- Subprocessor changes: we can contractually offer the "Residency Commitment" addendum that provides 60-day notice, monthly roster attestations, and a right to terminate if an EU-only replacement is not available in the notice window.
- Temporary cross-hop: default DR policy = 72-hour temporary cross-region processing window; any such event is recorded in the customer's audit trail with start/end timestamps and reason code. We can shorten the window to 24h for customers who require it but that will require a dedicated on-call and potentially a higher reserved capacity commitment.

Attachments included: redwood_dpa_v2.pdf (with addendum language), subprocessor_roster_jul2026.csv (current EU-only subprocessors flagged), pinning-playbook-draft.docx (ops steps, telemetry keys, and runbook templates).

Next steps: please confirm whether MedSys wants the Residency Commitment addendum and whether you require the 24h failover cap (we can include pricing for the shorter window in the SOW). If MedSys signs the addendum, we will lock the subprocessor notice terms and schedule an onboarding evidence call.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Customer Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v2.pdf (PDF, 125 KB) — contains addendum option; subprocessor_roster_jul2026.csv (CSV, 8 KB); pinning-playbook-draft.docx (DOCX, 42 KB)

Hi Irene / Ben / Marissa — thanks for the quick, precise response and the artifacts. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

1) We'll take the Residency Commitment addendum. Please send a redline of the DPA addendum with the 60-day notice + termination clause and we'll run it through procurement.

2) The 72h default is acceptable for now, but we would like pricing for the 24h cap as part of the SOW options. If the 24h option materially increases cost, flag that as an add-on.

3) For auditability, please confirm the log export format and retention: we prefer JSON lines with ISO timestamps and 12 months retention for cross-hop events.

If you can send the redline and a short SOW line-item for the 24h cap, we can aim to finalize the DPA next week.

Thanks — Anna

Anna Kaufmann
Sr. Privacy Counsel, MedSys Health
